title: Write-through and allocate
description: Where a store goes under *write-through*, and what changes when a store miss does not allocate.

steps.text: This cache is *write-through*: every store updates the line and memory together, so the two always agree and no line is ever dirty. On a store miss it also *allocates*: the line is brought into the cache first. The trace stores 7, then 8, to `0x0A4`, then loads it.
How many times will this trace write to memory?
options: Once, when the line leaves the cache
steps.explain: Twice. Under write-through each store goes to memory when it happens. The load writes nothing.
steps.hint: Under write-through, when does a store reach memory?
Press Run in the transport bar. If the trace has already run, press Reset, then Run.

steps.text: One miss, which allocated the line, then two hits. Write-throughs: 2, and memory holds 8. The cache never holds a value memory lacks, so a line can be dropped at any time without a write-back.
Set On a store miss to No allocate. The cache will ask to reset; choose Reset and apply.
steps.hint: On a store miss is in the bar above the cache. Pick No allocate.

steps.text: Under no-allocate, a store that misses writes memory and does not bring the line into the cache. Run the same trace. How many of the three accesses will hit?
steps.explain: None. Neither store allocates a line, so the second store misses too. The load then misses and is the first access to bring the line in.
steps.hint: Does the first store leave the line in the cache?
Press Run in the transport bar.

steps.text: Three misses and no hits. Write-arounds: 2, the stores that went around the cache straight to memory. Memory still ends at 8, so memory traffic is the same; what changed is that stores no longer fill the cache. No allocate pays off when a program writes data it will not read again soon.
